summary: Wallowa-Whitman 68-ft pole tower near Fish Lake, Baker County: built 1926, staffed to 1946, removed or destroyed 1953; remnants reported.

facts.design: 68-foot pole tower with a 6x6 cab, with a log cabin built alongside
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1953 (sources differ on which); some remnants were still visible per the Forest Lookouts page

staffing.status: staffed in the 1930s and 1940s per newspaper items quoted on the Forest Lookouts page

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower and log cabin were removed in 1953; firelookout.com and the Forest Lookouts page say destroyed. All three date the end to 1953, so the story reports both words.
The register places the site about a mile south of Fish Lake; firelookout.com gives 12 miles north of Halfway. Both are reference points, not a contradiction, and the story uses Fish Lake.

sources.title: Trinity Guard Station Fire Lookout Tower

notes_for_editor: Removed vs destroyed in 1953 is a wording conflict only. The register's 'about 1 miles south of Fish Lake' has a typo in the source (1 miles); the story says about a mile. Height 20.7 m is the brief's value and matches 68 ft. Access is not described by any source, so no access fact was written; the brief's unknown stands. The Forest Lookouts remnants line is undated. The 1946 staffing is the last staffed reference found; a 1947 social item names the Gentry family at Trinity lookout and was left out as unclear. No photos added.
